about: Sharing an umbrella in the rain

lines.text: The rain started just as I stepped out of the lift this morning.
I had left my umbrella in school, so I wait under the shelter
lines.note: Tense: the story is in the past, so it is 'waited'.

lines.text: with a dozen other people. Two small boy were splashing in a puddle while
their mother tried to keep them dry. An old man beside me were reading
lines.note: Agreement: 'an old man' is one person, so it is 'was'.

lines.text: a newspaper as if nothing unusual was happening. After ten minutes, the rain grew
heavier, and I began to worry about being late. Then a woman which lived
lines.note: Relative pronoun: a woman is a person, so it is 'who'.

lines.text: on my floor came down with a huge umbrella. She offered to share it
with me, and we walk to the bus stop together under it.
lines.note: Tense: 'offered … and we walked' — the story is in the past.

lines.text: She told me that she takes the same bus every day at a hour
lines.note: Article: 'hour' starts with a vowel sound, so it is 'an hour'.

lines.text: when most people are still asleep. My shoes was soaked by the time we
lines.note: Agreement: 'my shoes' is plural, so it is 'were'.

lines.text: arrived, but I reached school on time. I thanked her polite and promised to
lines.note: Word form: 'thanked' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'politely'.

lines.text: carry my own umbrella every day from now on.
